proposed_content: Harmonic and geometric families reach the same Sato–Tate interface by different measure-producing mechanisms: the trace formula isolates a Plancherel main term and pushes it through an L-group representation, whereas residue-class localization and Deligne–Katz equidistribution push Haar measure from geometric monodromy through the fiber representation.

proposed_content: How much twisting or averaging varies controls what family statistics forget: quadratic scalar averaging retains the even trace information and can leave the individual Sato–Tate problem intact, while averaging over the full circle annihilates the self-duality indicators and forces unitary type; separately, sparse conductor exhaustions can prevent a vertical Sato–Tate limit even when low-zero universality persists.

proposed_content: Fixed-degree geometric cohomology is transported into an automorphic family through a chain of representation changes: local Weil–Deligne data preserve Euler factors and conductors under local Langlands, conjectural global reciprocity supplies an automorphic representation, and the degree-dependent determinant twist removes pure cohomological weight to place good-reduction local parameters on the unitary axis.
